prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, from bifunctional PROTACs to the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-type molecular glue degraders.

statement.case_for: I keep B057 as a single-part prize with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The shared chemical idea is that a small molecule can act as a catalytic bridge that brings a target to an E3 ligase, so removal of the target replaces occupancy of a site. The Crews and Deshaies PROTAC work established the concept and first demonstrations. Handa's identification of cereblon explains how thalidomide-type drugs act, and that is what makes the glue strand part of the same induced-proximity story. The mechanism has been reproduced across many laboratories, ligases and target classes. On the timing question the chair raised, I do not think a prize has to wait for an approved drug when the mechanism and its generality are confirmed independently. The prize record contains awards for methods and concepts whose clinical payoff came later. I accept this is a judgement about maturity and I state it as such. My position has not changed since round 1, but the round-1 exchange sharpened my reasons.
statement.case_against: No degrader is approved, so the committee could be criticised for rewarding promise. The three-name cap leaves out Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Ito and Kim, and each has a real claim. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures turned PROTAC design into a rational chemical problem, which I value as a physical chemist. The PROTAC and glue strands also have different histories, and one citation could be accused of blurring them. If the committee concludes that the strands cannot be fairly joined, or that the field is a few years early, B054 is the more settled fallback, and its credit problem (Mehl and Yokoyama) is smaller than the B057 one.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers B054 and still treats Handa versus Ciulli as unsettled, arguing that Ciulli's VHL and ternary-complex work made PROTACs drug-like.
responses.response: I answer the chair's third-laureate question by keeping Handa, and I give my reason. If Ciulli replaced Handa, the citation would have to narrow to PROTACs, and the cereblon result that explains thalidomide would be left unattributed. That would remove the one piece of mechanism that unites the two arms. I accept that Ciulli's structural work is real and that the omission is a cost. I would rather state that cost openly than narrow the citation. If Brzezinski prefers a PROTAC-only citation with Ciulli, I would want that to be a deliberate choice about scope and not a way to avoid the glue question. I do not think his B054 preference is unreasonable, and it is my first fallback.

responses.point: Somfai prefers B068 (Buchwald and Hartwig) for its maturity and clean two-person credit, and argues that the 2010 prize covered C-C coupling and not C-N coupling.
responses.response: I accept that the 2010 prize covered C-C bond formation and that the catalytic, ligand-controlled C-N method is a real advance with clean attribution. Zou's wording, that the citation should name the catalytic, general method, handles Kosugi well enough for me. My remaining difference is about novelty of concept. B068 refines a recognised way of making bonds, whereas induced proximity changes what a small molecule does in a cell. I also agree with Somfai that B057 has a harder attribution problem, and that is why I list B068 as an alternative. I would not oppose it on merit if B057 fails to reach a majority.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, prefers the same B057 configuration but concedes that credit is spread over at least eight people and that the PROTAC and glue strands have different histories.
responses.response: I agree that the strands have different histories, and I do not wish to hide that. My answer to his worry that one citation blurs two achievements is that the citation names both and says what links them, which is recruitment of an E3 ligase by a small molecule. I would not support splitting B057 into two parts. Each part would then rest on fewer people and a thinner argument, and I think that would make the credit problem worse. A single part with a precise citation is the more honest form, even though it leaves out named contributors.

responses.point: Zou prefers B068 but says she would support B057 if the clinical evidence is judged sufficient, and in her round-1 file she raised a two-part split of B057.
responses.response: I take her condition seriously. The clinical evidence is incomplete, and I will not claim otherwise. My view is that the scientific evidence that matters for this prize is the mechanism, which is confirmed, and its reproducibility across many laboratories and target classes. Late-stage trials do add weight, but they are not the basis of my vote. I would also ask her to say plainly whether the absence of an approved drug is a reason she would withhold a vote or only a reservation she would accept.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept the absence of an approved degrader as no obstacle to a prize.
Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name, and whether any three-name cap fairly represents the PROTAC and glue lineages.
Whether the single citation is precise enough that it does not conflate two distinct discoveries.
Whether, if B057 does not reach five votes, the committee prefers B054 or B068 as its fallback.
statement.conflict_note: No recusal-level conflict. I am at Lund with Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, a shared institution and not a tie to any candidate. My research on lipid self-assembly, lipid-protein co-assembly and membranes overlaps scientifically with B005 and B064, which I ranked first and second in the opening. I disclose this because it could colour my judgement of those ballots. My preferred configuration, B057, and my alternatives, B054 and B068, have no such connection. This disclosure is unchanged from round 1 and no member has requested recusal.
